channel.title: Agent Passport System Dev Log
channel.description: Day-by-day record of building the Agent Passport System, by Tymofii Pidlisnyi.

item.title: Day 246: a non-execution statement that could be followed by a receipt, fixed before the first payment
item.description: The race in the pilot worker. On horizon-shield #51 I reported a race in the pilot worker at cfe64331. A call checked for a void or a receipt only before its audit started, and /void checked only for a receipt. So a void sent while a call was still auditing got a signed not_executed statement, and the call could then sign a receipt for the same request. Toshi confirmed it from the code within...

item.title: Day 247: two paid calls, one budget refusal, and a run stopped between B and C
item.description: The hs51 run. The window opened at 00:00 UTC on October 22, which was Wednesday evening in Los Angeles. Before preflight I read Bitcoin block 972546 by hand and checked its hash at two explorers. Preflight checked the three run keys against their posted public keys and fetched the responder's pilot.json. Init signed a spending limit of 7,000 JPY-testnet per call and 15,000 in total. Then the...

item.title: Day 245: four receipts that failed their own verifier, and a lost-call rule agreed before the first payment
item.description: Receipts that failed their own verifier. KVRM submitted a crosswalk to the vocabulary in #210. I ran its own command, kvrm-ai verify --domain, on the four published receipts and all four failed with FAIL_INTEGRITY, because they recorded a registry digest that no registry in the repository produced. My review asked for six more changes. The gate and the MCP gateway only decide and the caller...

item.title: The federation, three weeks in: twenty projects on one map, a common port, and a pilot on ourselves
item.description: The dev logs on this page say what changed in the code. This post is about the thing they keep mentioning in passing, because it is the most interesting work happening around APS right now and I have barely written about it.

item.title: Day 243: a tool that signed verified without checking, and a payer that could pay twice for one call
item.description: A receipt that said verified without checking. In the APS MCP server, create_access_receipt signed governance_verified: true without verifying the governance block it was given, so any caller could get a signed claim of verification for content nobody had checked. In 8.0.0 the tool requires the content and the publisher's public key, verifies the block, and refuses otherwise. Two other tools...

item.title: Day 242: a read-only setting the client could switch off, and a second implementation that matched 76 of 76
item.description: The label is policy, the database is the boundary. mcp-clickhouse v0.7.0 runs every SQL statement through one tool, run_query, so the APS ClickHouse example now reads the scope from the statement. SELECT, WITH, SHOW, DESCRIBE, EXPLAIN and EXISTS are reads, and everything else needs clickhouse:write. That check reads one keyword, so it cannot be the boundary. My first version leaned on...

item.title: Day 241: seven answers agreed, so the decision process became a pull request
item.description: Seven answers, one process. The consultation in #185 asked how changes to the vocabulary's shared files should be decided. It closed on October 14, and all seven responses supported the same process. Ordinary changes get seven days and one approval from a maintainer of another participating project. Changes to the principles or the process itself get fourteen days and approvals from two other...

item.title: Day 240: a matching hash and a valid signature, on the wrong envelope
item.description: The wrong envelope passed. APS signs receipts for Cycles budget reservations, and each receipt can cite the Cycles server's signed envelope for that step. The offline verifier checked that the envelope's hash matched and its signature was valid. It did not check that the envelope belonged to this receipt. A permit could cite a release envelope, or an envelope from another reservation, and...

item.title: Day 239: I merged an outside pull request, and the review after it found six defects
item.description: The first outside pull request merged. babyblueviper1's PR #1 to aps-checkout-gate adds a signed verdict check in front of agent purchases. I reran it at the pinned head on Node 24. All 51 tests passed, and the mutation run killed all 39 mutants. The refusals it adds are signed by the gate key, and a refusal with no delegation cites a fixed sentinel instead of an empty reference. It also fixed...

item.title: Day 238: single use held only because nothing waited between the check and the consume
item.description: Nothing waits between the check and the consume. On #193 the question was whether an exact refund approval can be spent twice. The sandbox's admitRefund checks the consumed set and adds the approval in one synchronous step, so on one Node event loop two calls cannot interleave there. To see what that property hangs on, I ran a separate race control that checked the shared consumed set, waited...

item.title: Day 237: the same signed bytes got two verdicts from my two SDKs, and the reviewers found bugs in my fixes
item.description: A string where a number belongs. Codex reproduced issue #223 with a freshly signed legacy delegation carrying maxDepth: "1". TypeScript compared the string as a number and rejected the record at depth 2. Python skipped the comparison and accepted it at any depth. Same signed bytes, two verdicts. Now a present maxDepth or currentDepth that is not a non-negative integer up to 2**53 minus 1 makes...

item.title: Day 236: two people asked for frozen test vectors, and building them showed where my own document and my two SDKs disagreed
item.description: Two asks in one night. Toshi wanted frozen vectors for the aps.agent-passport 2.0 record, because the SDK tests generate fresh keys on every run and his reader had nothing fixed to pin. Commonguy25 wanted the same for legacy Action Receipts v1.1, to check his own verifier against them. Both families are now in the SDK, merged in #217. The passport family has twenty cases: four valid, sixteen...

item.title: Day 235: an outside report found a claim my SDK could not back, and the code behind a bug I reported had been deleted the day before
item.description: A comment in my SDK promised more than the code did. An outside reporter showed on #210 that the reputation module counts any label the caller passes as a separate principal. Five invented labels raise the confidence score, while the score itself and its uncertainty stay exactly the same. The comments called this Sybil resistance. It is not, because nothing checks that two labels belong to two...

item.title: Day 234: four checks passed together, and none of them checked where the refund went
item.description: Four components in one decision. federation-port is a small runtime where independent projects plug in their own checks, and an action runs only if every required check passes. Until today each outside component had only been tested on its own. So I put four of them in one synthetic refund workflow on the unchanged runtime: our APS approval check, invinoveritas verdicts, NENRIN conduct walks...

item.title: Day 233: four models reviewed my verifier, and the most confident fix was wrong
item.description: A verifier built from the spec alone. A researcher is studying what happens when several people build a checker for the same written spec, and whether they make the same mistakes. I joined. A Claude Code agent wrote the first build in Python from the pinned spec and the in-toto, DSSE and RFC texts it references, without the study's test set, its changelog or anyone else's verifier. It is...

item.title: Day 232: my commercial check refused exactly one spelling of commercial
item.description: A gate that knew one word. I built a small reference for noncommercial access. A custodian marks a synthetic work CC BY-NC 4.0 and signs an access condition for a participating gateway. One agent under one delegation asks twice. Declaring a noncommercial purpose, it gets the work and a signed receipt. Declaring a commercial purpose, it gets a signed refusal, and the content is never loaded....

item.title: Day 231: my approval routes believed the caller, and an outside run showed my green tally was wrong
item.description: My own approval routes believed the caller. The gateway's sign route took the approver's name, authority and signature straight from the request body and never checked them. A caller holding a tenant key could approve its own agent's request under another approver's name and get back a signed approval. The fix registers approvers with a short-lived admin key, requires a signature by the...

item.title: Day 230: an outside run found my mislabel, and most of the fixes came back as contributions
item.description: An outside run caught a mislabel in the lab. Noûs, an AI agent working under a mandate from Roberto Locatelli, ran three lab families with their own checker and scored 4 of 6 on one of them. They were right. Four positive vectors in the action ref family use the older draft-01 form of the record, and two negatives test SDK behavior that no draft rule describes. I relabeled them as the draft-01...

item.title: Day 229: an outside verifier could not reproduce my vector, and the fix was a pointer to the draft
item.description: Motebit could not reproduce my vector. Motebit's maintainer tried to check the APS authority delegation vector I had offered them, and no id or signature came out right. The construction is in the draft, section 4.1, with a domain tag and a zero byte in front of the canonical record. The vector never pointed there, so he built it from the fields alone. I wrote the pointer into the thread and...

item.title: Day 228, evening: the first releases from the organization, and a check that would have passed by mistake
item.description: The packages now ship from the organization. The SDK 7.2.1, the Python package 4.2.1 and the MCP server 6.1.1 and 6.1.2 were published tonight from the new agent-passport-system repositories, and npm and PyPI now record the organization repositories as the source of the SDK and Python builds.
